title: Ovarian Cancer
subtitle: StewardMD ONCOTREE navigator (draft)
provenanceNote: ONCOTREE navigator DRAFT for epithelial ovarian / fallopian-tube / primary-peritoneal cancer. Full pathway: workup -> setting -> histology -> molecular testing -> FIGO stage / risk -> primary debulking vs neoadjuvant (with a response-adapted interval-debulking step) -> platinum-taxane +/- bevacizumab -> biomarker-directed first-line maintenance -> surveillance, then a line-of-therapy recurrence sub-tree keyed to the platinum-free interval (sensitive -> doublet -> relapse maintenance -> second relapse; resistant -> FRalpha-directed; refractory). Low-grade serous, mucinous, and non-epithelial tumors follow their own arms. Each systemic-therapy treatment leaf routes to APPLICABLE StewardMD Standard Protocols by reference (shared gyn- backbones plus disease-scoped ov- DRAFT single-agent / regimen protocols: PLD, weekly paclitaxel, topotecan, gemcitabine, single-agent carboplatin, mirvetuximab, letrozole endocrine, trametinib MEK, BEP); surgery-only and pure observation / best-supportive-care leaves carry no dose protocol and are shown as checklist guidance. Workup / staging / risk / biomarker / surveillance content is standard oncology, authored in StewardMD's words, not proprietary guideline text; structural pathway consistent with Standard Guidelines (NCCN), DeVita, Harrison. Invents no dose/regimen/criterion. DRAFT - not clinically activated; the physician decides and the existing dose engine computes patient doses.
sourceNote: Structural pathway consistent with Standard Guidelines (NCCN Ovarian Cancer), DeVita, Harrison. Regimen options reference existing StewardMD Standard Protocols; the dose engine computes patient doses.

a.text: Carboplatin (AUC 5-6) + paclitaxel every 3 weeks for 6 cycles is the standard first-line backbone for epithelial ovarian cancer; dose-dense weekly paclitaxel and intraperitoneal schedules are accepted alternatives in selected patients.

b.text: Bevacizumab added to chemotherapy and continued as maintenance improves progression-free survival in advanced disease; reserve for higher-risk / stage IV / suboptimally debulked patients and screen for perforation, bleeding, hypertension, and impaired wound healing.

c.text: PARP-inhibitor maintenance after response to first-line platinum gives the largest benefit in BRCA-mutant (olaparib) and HRD-positive (niraparib, or olaparib + bevacizumab) tumors; niraparib is also active regardless of biomarker with a smaller benefit.

d.text: Platinum-free interval (time from last platinum to relapse) approximates platinum sensitivity: at least 6 months = platinum-sensitive, under 6 months = platinum-resistant, progression on platinum = platinum-refractory. It is a continuum and a clinical guide, not a hard rule.

e.text: Folate-receptor-alpha (FRalpha) expression selects platinum-resistant patients for mirvetuximab soravtansine; screen for and prophylax against ocular toxicity (keratopathy) with baseline and periodic ophthalmologic review.

nodes.name: Initial workup
nodes.title: Initial workup and diagnosis
nodes.description: Baseline evaluation of a suspected ovarian / fallopian-tube / primary-peritoneal cancer before treatment planning.
bullets: History, physical and pelvic exam; performance status; family cancer history
Pelvic / transvaginal ultrasound and CT chest-abdomen-pelvis to characterize the adnexal mass, ascites, and omental / peritoneal disease
CA-125 (add CEA / CA19-9 if a GI or mucinous primary is possible) as a baseline for response and surveillance
Tissue diagnosis: histology and grade from surgery, or image-guided biopsy / paracentesis if neoadjuvant chemotherapy is planned
Germline and tumor BRCA1/2 + HRD testing with genetic counseling; refer for gynecologic-oncology surgical assessment before any intervention

nodes.name: Clinical setting
nodes.title: Clinical setting
nodes.description: Choose the current clinical state; management diverges sharply between newly diagnosed, recurrent, and surveillance settings.

nodes.name: Histology
nodes.title: Histologic subtype
nodes.description: Epithelial subtype drives systemic therapy. High-grade serous is the dominant type and follows the main platinum-taxane pathway; low-grade serous, mucinous, and non-epithelial tumors follow distinct routes.
bullets: High-grade epithelial (serous, endometrioid, clear cell, carcinosarcoma): most chemo-responsive, main pathway
Low-grade serous: indolent, relatively chemo-resistant, hormone-receptor driven
Mucinous: rule out a GI primary; distinct chemosensitivity
Non-epithelial (germ-cell / sex-cord stromal): entirely different management

options.label: High-grade epithelial (serous / endometrioid / clear cell / carcinosarcoma)

nodes.name: Molecular testing
nodes.title: Molecular / biomarker testing
nodes.description: For high-grade epithelial disease, complete biomarker testing early - the results select maintenance and later-line therapy. Testing does not change the primary chemotherapy backbone.
bullets: BRCA1/2 germline AND tumor (somatic): strongest predictor of PARP-inhibitor benefit
Homologous-recombination deficiency (HRD) assay: genomic-instability / scar score in BRCA wild-type tumors
Folate-receptor-alpha (FRalpha) expression: predicts mirvetuximab benefit in platinum-resistant relapse
Mismatch-repair / MSI and HER2 where relevant (endometrioid, clear cell)

nodes.name: FIGO stage
nodes.title: FIGO stage
nodes.description: Surgical-pathologic FIGO stage separates disease confined to the ovaries (early) from disease spread within or beyond the pelvis (advanced), which drives surgery and systemic therapy.

tables.title: FIGO stage (simplified)
rows: Confined to one or both ovaries / tubes
Pelvic extension or primary peritoneal disease within the pelvis
Peritoneal spread beyond the pelvis and/or retroperitoneal nodes
Distant metastasis (positive pleural effusion cytology, parenchymal / extra-abdominal)

nodes.name: Early-stage risk
nodes.title: Stage I: risk stratification
nodes.description: In stage I disease, grade, substage, rupture / surface involvement, and histology determine whether adjuvant chemotherapy is added after complete surgical staging.

tables.title: Stage I adjuvant-risk features
rows: Stage IA or IB, grade 1, non-clear-cell, capsule intact
Stage IC, grade 2-3, clear-cell histology, surface involvement or rupture

options.label: High risk (IC, grade 2-3, or clear cell)

nodes.name: Early low-risk observation
nodes.title: Stage IA/IB grade 1: surgery alone
nodes.description: Comprehensive surgical staging is definitive for low-risk stage I disease; adjuvant chemotherapy is not required.
bullets: Complete surgical staging (hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, omentectomy, peritoneal / nodal sampling)
No adjuvant chemotherapy for stage IA/IB grade 1
Fertility-sparing unilateral salpingo-oophorectomy is an option for stage IA in a young patient wanting fertility
Enter routine surveillance

nodes.title: Stage I high-risk: adjuvant platinum-taxane
nodes.name: Early high-risk chemo
nodes.description: High-risk stage I disease benefits from adjuvant carboplatin-paclitaxel after complete surgical staging, then surveillance.
bullets: Complete surgical staging first
Adjuvant carboplatin + paclitaxel; 3-6 cycles (often 6 for clear-cell / grade 3 / stage IC)
Bevacizumab and PARP maintenance are generally not used for fully resected stage I disease
Enter surveillance after treatment

nodes.name: Surgical approach
nodes.title: Advanced disease: surgical approach
nodes.description: For stage II-IV disease, decide between upfront primary debulking and neoadjuvant chemotherapy with interval debulking, based on resectability and fitness. The goal either way is no residual macroscopic disease (R0).
bullets: Primary debulking: preferred when complete cytoreduction to R0 looks achievable and the patient is fit
Neoadjuvant chemotherapy: bulky unresectable disease, poor performance status, or high surgical risk; requires a tissue diagnosis first
Not a surgical / chemo candidate: very poor performance status - palliative approach

options.label: Not a candidate for surgery or intensive chemo

nodes.name: Primary debulking + chemo
nodes.title: Primary debulking then adjuvant platinum-taxane
nodes.description: Complete cytoreduction followed by adjuvant carboplatin-paclitaxel, with bevacizumab added for higher-risk disease. Proceed to maintenance selection at chemotherapy completion.
bullets: Maximal-effort cytoreduction to no visible residual disease (R0) by gynecologic oncology
Adjuvant carboplatin + paclitaxel every 3 weeks for 6 cycles
Add and continue bevacizumab for stage IV / suboptimal debulking / high-risk disease
Assess response by exam, CA-125, and imaging, then select maintenance (next step)

nodes.name: Neoadjuvant chemo
nodes.title: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy (pre-surgery)
nodes.description: Neoadjuvant carboplatin-paclitaxel, typically 3 cycles, then restage to decide on interval debulking. Response drives the next step.
bullets: Neoadjuvant carboplatin + paclitaxel, usually 3 cycles, then reassess resectability
Bevacizumab is generally NOT given in the cycles immediately around surgery (wound healing)
Restage with CA-125 and imaging to judge response
Then a response-adapted decision on interval debulking (next step)

nodes.name: Neoadjuvant response
nodes.title: Response after neoadjuvant chemotherapy
nodes.description: Restaging after neoadjuvant chemotherapy determines whether interval debulking proceeds or the systemic strategy changes.
bullets: Responding / resectable: proceed to interval debulking surgery, then complete chemotherapy
Stable but resectable: interval debulking may still benefit selected patients
Progression / not resectable: switch systemic therapy or move to palliative goals

nodes.name: Interval debulking + chemo
nodes.title: Interval debulking then completion chemotherapy
nodes.description: Responders undergo interval debulking to R0, then complete carboplatin-paclitaxel (about 6 total cycles), then maintenance selection.
bullets: Interval debulking surgery to no visible residual disease (R0)
Complete carboplatin + paclitaxel to about 6 total cycles
May start / continue bevacizumab after wound healing for high-risk disease
Assess response, then select maintenance (next step)

nodes.name: Neoadjuvant non-responder
nodes.title: Progression on neoadjuvant chemotherapy: change strategy
nodes.description: Progression through platinum-based neoadjuvant chemotherapy is platinum-refractory behavior; change systemic therapy and reassess surgical candidacy and goals of care.
bullets: Progression on platinum neoadjuvant therapy signals platinum resistance / refractoriness
Switch to a non-platinum single agent (with bevacizumab where appropriate) or a clinical trial
Interval debulking is generally deferred unless a meaningful response is achieved
Early palliative care and goals-of-care discussion; still assess maintenance if disease is controlled (next step)

nodes.name: Palliative
nodes.title: Not a surgical / intensive-chemo candidate: palliative care
nodes.description: For patients too frail for cytoreduction or full-dose platinum-taxane, prioritize symptom control with gentle, individualized systemic options.
bullets: Early palliative-care involvement; manage ascites, bowel obstruction, and pain
Consider single-agent carboplatin or attenuated dosing if any systemic therapy is pursued
Reassess fitness - a good response may make interval surgery or fuller chemotherapy possible
Goals-of-care discussion

nodes.name: Maintenance biomarker
nodes.title: First-line maintenance: BRCA / HRD status
nodes.description: After response to first-line platinum, maintenance is selected by BRCA and HRD status and by whether bevacizumab was already part of chemotherapy.

tables.title: First-line maintenance by biomarker
rows: PARP inhibitor (olaparib); add bevacizumab if already started
Complete response, low risk, no bevacizumab

options.label: Complete response, low risk - consider observation

nodes.name: BRCA maintenance
nodes.title: Maintenance, BRCA-mutant: PARP inhibitor
nodes.description: BRCA-mutant tumors derive the greatest benefit from first-line PARP-inhibitor maintenance after response to platinum, then surveillance.
bullets: Olaparib maintenance (or niraparib) after response to first-line platinum
If bevacizumab was part of chemotherapy, olaparib + bevacizumab is an option
Monitor CBC for myelosuppression; counsel on secondary-malignancy risk
Then enter surveillance (next step)

nodes.name: HRD maintenance
nodes.title: Maintenance, HRD-positive (BRCA wild-type): PARP inhibitor
nodes.description: HRD-positive, BRCA wild-type tumors still benefit substantially from PARP-inhibitor maintenance, with or without bevacizumab, then surveillance.
bullets: Niraparib maintenance, or olaparib + bevacizumab if bevacizumab was used with chemotherapy
Benefit is intermediate between BRCA-mutant and HR-proficient disease
Monitor CBC and blood pressure (if on bevacizumab)
Then enter surveillance (next step)

nodes.name: HR-proficient maintenance
nodes.title: Maintenance, HR-proficient: bevacizumab or niraparib
nodes.description: In HR-proficient / HRD-negative disease PARP benefit is small; bevacizumab maintenance (if started with chemo) or niraparib are the usual choices, then surveillance.
bullets: Bevacizumab maintenance if it was part of chemotherapy
Niraparib maintenance is an option regardless of biomarker but with smaller benefit here
Observation is reasonable for a complete responder who did not receive bevacizumab
Then enter surveillance (next step)

nodes.name: Maintenance observation
nodes.title: Observation after first-line therapy
nodes.description: For a complete responder at low risk who did not receive bevacizumab and has no PARP indication, active surveillance is acceptable.
bullets: No maintenance drug; monitor closely
Reconfirm BRCA / HRD results are complete before defaulting to observation
Then enter routine surveillance (next step)

nodes.name: Surveillance
nodes.title: Post-treatment surveillance
nodes.description: Monitoring after completion of therapy; a rising CA-125 or symptoms prompt imaging and entry into the recurrence pathway.
bullets: History, exam and pelvic exam every 2-4 months for 2 years, then less frequently to 5 years, then annually
CA-125 at each visit if initially elevated; imaging (CT) for a rising CA-125 or symptoms
Counsel that treating an asymptomatic CA-125-only rise earlier has not improved survival - individualize
Address survivorship and cascade genetic testing of relatives if BRCA-positive
A confirmed relapse enters the recurrence pathway (next step)

nodes.name: Platinum-free interval
nodes.title: Recurrence: platinum-free interval
nodes.description: At relapse, the interval from the last platinum dose to progression approximates platinum sensitivity and directs the whole recurrence strategy.

tables.title: Platinum-free interval categories
rows: Re-treat with a platinum doublet; consider secondary surgery
Non-platinum single agent +/- bevacizumab; biomarker options
Poor prognosis; trial / single agent / supportive care

nodes.name: Platinum-sensitive path
nodes.title: Platinum-sensitive relapse: strategy
nodes.description: For platinum-sensitive relapse, decide on secondary cytoreduction and account for any prior PARP exposure before choosing the platinum doublet.
bullets: Secondary cytoreduction: consider for isolated / oligometastatic relapse, good performance status, long platinum-free interval, and likely complete resection
Chemo, no prior PARP: platinum doublet then PARP or bevacizumab maintenance
Chemo, prior PARP: platinum doublet, favor bevacizumab maintenance

nodes.name: Secondary cytoreduction
nodes.title: Platinum-sensitive: secondary surgery + platinum doublet
nodes.description: Selected platinum-sensitive relapses benefit from secondary cytoreduction to R0 followed by a platinum-based doublet, then relapse maintenance.
bullets: Secondary cytoreduction when complete resection is likely (favorable selection)
Platinum-based doublet after surgery: carboplatin + paclitaxel, carboplatin + liposomal doxorubicin, or carboplatin + gemcitabine
PLD and gemcitabine partners have no dose protocol here - physician arranges those regimens
Then choose relapse maintenance on response (next step)

nodes.name: Platinum doublet
nodes.title: Platinum-sensitive: platinum doublet (no prior PARP)
nodes.description: Platinum-sensitive relapse without prior PARP maintenance is re-treated with a platinum doublet, then relapse maintenance on response.
bullets: Platinum doublet: carboplatin + paclitaxel, carboplatin + liposomal doxorubicin, or carboplatin + gemcitabine (+/- bevacizumab)
Add bevacizumab where not contraindicated
PLD and gemcitabine partners have no dose protocol here - physician arranges those regimens
Then choose relapse maintenance on response (next step)

nodes.name: Post-PARP platinum doublet
nodes.title: Platinum-sensitive after prior PARP: platinum doublet
nodes.description: When PARP maintenance was already used, re-treat with a platinum doublet and favor bevacizumab maintenance; repeat PARP has limited added benefit.
bullets: Platinum doublet as above, ideally with bevacizumab
Repeat PARP maintenance gives limited benefit after prior PARP - individualize
Re-biopsy / re-test at relapse if it will change therapy
Then choose relapse maintenance on response (next step)

nodes.name: Relapse maintenance
nodes.title: Maintenance after platinum-sensitive relapse
nodes.description: After response to a platinum doublet at relapse, choose maintenance by prior PARP exposure and by whether bevacizumab was used.

nodes.name: Relapse PARP maintenance
nodes.title: Platinum-sensitive relapse: PARP maintenance
nodes.description: PARP-inhibitor maintenance after response to a platinum doublet in a PARP-naive patient prolongs progression-free survival.
bullets: Olaparib or niraparib maintenance after response, if not previously given
Largest benefit in BRCA-mutant / HRD-positive relapse
Monitor CBC; counsel on secondary-malignancy risk
Treat progression as a new relapse (next step)

nodes.name: Relapse bevacizumab maintenance
nodes.title: Platinum-sensitive relapse: bevacizumab maintenance
nodes.description: Bevacizumab maintenance after a platinum doublet is preferred when PARP was already used or PARP benefit is small.
bullets: Continue bevacizumab as maintenance if it was part of the doublet
Preferred after prior PARP maintenance or in HR-proficient disease
Monitor blood pressure, proteinuria, and bleeding / perforation risk
Treat progression as a new relapse (next step)

nodes.name: Relapse observation
nodes.title: Platinum-sensitive relapse: observation
nodes.description: Observation is reasonable after a good response when no maintenance is indicated or tolerated.
bullets: No maintenance drug; close monitoring with CA-125 and imaging
Reasonable when maintenance is not tolerated or the benefit is judged small
Treat progression as a new relapse (next step)

nodes.name: Second relapse
nodes.title: Second relapse: re-assess platinum sensitivity
nodes.description: At the next progression, re-assess the platinum-free interval - sensitivity usually shortens with each line - and choose therapy accordingly.

nodes.name: Second-relapse platinum
nodes.title: Second relapse, still platinum-sensitive: another platinum doublet
nodes.description: A still-sensitive second relapse is re-treated with a platinum doublet, with maintenance individualized by prior exposure and tolerance.
bullets: Another platinum doublet (carboplatin + paclitaxel / PLD / gemcitabine, +/- bevacizumab)
Watch cumulative toxicity and carboplatin hypersensitivity; premedicate / desensitize as needed
Individualize maintenance by prior PARP / bevacizumab exposure
Continue surveillance and re-assess at each progression

nodes.name: Second-relapse resistant
nodes.title: Second relapse, now platinum-resistant: non-platinum therapy
nodes.description: A second relapse that is now platinum-resistant is managed as platinum-resistant disease with sequential non-platinum agents and biomarker-directed options.
bullets: Sequential non-platinum single agents: PLD, weekly paclitaxel, topotecan, or gemcitabine (+/- bevacizumab)
Mirvetuximab soravtansine for FRalpha-high disease
No dose protocol for these single agents here - physician arranges the regimen
Prioritize quality of life and clinical trials

nodes.name: Platinum-resistant biomarker
nodes.title: Platinum-resistant relapse: FRalpha status
nodes.description: In platinum-resistant disease, folate-receptor-alpha expression selects patients for mirvetuximab; others receive sequential single-agent non-platinum chemotherapy.
bullets: FRalpha-high: mirvetuximab soravtansine (antibody-drug conjugate) option
FRalpha-low / unknown: sequential single-agent chemotherapy +/- bevacizumab

nodes.name: Mirvetuximab
nodes.title: Platinum-resistant, FRalpha-high: mirvetuximab
nodes.description: Folate-receptor-alpha-high platinum-resistant disease can be treated with mirvetuximab soravtansine.
bullets: Mirvetuximab soravtansine for FRalpha-high, platinum-resistant relapse (typically 1-3 prior regimens)
Baseline and periodic ophthalmologic exam; prophylactic eye care for keratopathy
No dose protocol here - physician arranges the regimen
Reassess and continue surveillance after treatment

nodes.name: Platinum-resistant chemo
nodes.title: Platinum-resistant: sequential single-agent chemo
nodes.description: Platinum-resistant disease is treated with sequential non-platinum single agents, with bevacizumab added where appropriate; goals are palliative.
bullets: Single-agent non-platinum: pegylated liposomal doxorubicin, weekly paclitaxel, topotecan, or gemcitabine
Add bevacizumab to single-agent chemo where not contraindicated (improves PFS)
Rotate agents sequentially on progression; avoid re-challenging with platinum
No dose protocol for these single agents here - physician arranges the regimen

nodes.name: Platinum-refractory
nodes.title: Platinum-refractory: trial / single agent / supportive care
nodes.description: Progression during platinum carries a poor prognosis; prioritize clinical trials, gentle single-agent therapy, and supportive care.
bullets: Strongly favor clinical-trial enrollment
Single-agent non-platinum chemotherapy +/- bevacizumab if performance status permits
Early palliative care; goals-of-care discussion
No dose protocol for these agents here - physician arranges the regimen

nodes.name: Low-grade serous surgery
nodes.title: Low-grade serous: maximal cytoreductive surgery
nodes.description: Low-grade serous carcinoma is indolent and relatively platinum-resistant; maximal surgery is the mainstay, then an adjuvant decision.
bullets: Maximal cytoreductive surgery to R0 is the mainstay
Chemotherapy responses are lower than in high-grade disease; hormone-receptor expression is common
Complete surgical staging and estrogen / progesterone-receptor testing
Then decide on adjuvant / maintenance strategy (next step)

nodes.name: Low-grade serous adjuvant
nodes.title: Low-grade serous: adjuvant strategy
nodes.description: After surgery for low-grade serous carcinoma, choose between endocrine maintenance and observation by stage, residual disease, and receptor status.

nodes.name: Low-grade serous endocrine
nodes.title: Low-grade serous: endocrine maintenance
nodes.description: Aromatase-inhibitor endocrine maintenance is favored in hormone-receptor-positive low-grade serous carcinoma after surgery.
bullets: Aromatase inhibitor (e.g. letrozole) maintenance given frequent hormone-receptor positivity
Bone-health monitoring on an aromatase inhibitor
No dose protocol for endocrine therapy here - physician arranges the regimen
Treat progression on the low-grade recurrence step (next step)

nodes.name: Low-grade serous observation
nodes.title: Low-grade serous: observation after surgery
nodes.description: Fully resected low-grade serous disease may be observed, especially when receptor-negative or early-stage.
bullets: Observation after complete resection, particularly early-stage / receptor-negative disease
Monitor with exam, CA-125, and imaging
Treat progression on the low-grade recurrence step (next step)

nodes.name: Low-grade serous recurrence
nodes.title: Low-grade serous: recurrence therapy
nodes.description: Recurrent low-grade serous carcinoma is directed by receptor status and MAPK-pathway targeting rather than intensive chemotherapy.

nodes.name: Low-grade serous MEK
nodes.title: Recurrent low-grade serous: MEK inhibitor
nodes.description: MEK inhibition targets frequent MAPK-pathway activation in recurrent low-grade serous carcinoma.
bullets: MEK inhibitor (e.g. trametinib) for recurrent low-grade serous disease
Monitor for rash, ocular changes, cardiac (ejection-fraction) and hepatic effects
No dose protocol here - physician arranges the regimen
Continue surveillance and re-assess at progression

nodes.name: Low-grade serous endocrine relapse
nodes.title: Recurrent low-grade serous: endocrine therapy
nodes.description: Endocrine therapy is a well-tolerated option for hormone-receptor-positive recurrent low-grade serous carcinoma.
bullets: Aromatase inhibitor or other endocrine therapy for receptor-positive disease
Well tolerated; reasonable for low-volume, indolent relapse
No dose protocol here - physician arranges the regimen
Continue surveillance and re-assess at progression

nodes.name: Low-grade serous chemo
nodes.title: Recurrent low-grade serous: platinum-based chemotherapy
nodes.description: Platinum-based chemotherapy is used for symptomatic or bulky recurrent low-grade serous disease despite lower response rates.
bullets: Carboplatin + paclitaxel for symptomatic / bulky relapse
Response rates are lower than in high-grade serous disease; individualize
Consider endocrine or MEK-directed maintenance after response
Continue surveillance and re-assess at progression

nodes.name: Mucinous workup
nodes.title: Mucinous: exclude a GI primary, then stage
nodes.description: Primary mucinous ovarian carcinoma is uncommon; first exclude a metastatic GI primary, then treat by stage.
bullets: Rule out a GI (appendiceal / colorectal / pancreaticobiliary) primary: endoscopy, CEA / CA19-9, imaging
Complete surgical staging including appendectomy
Confirm a true ovarian mucinous primary before adjuvant planning

nodes.name: Mucinous early
nodes.title: Mucinous, early-stage: surgery, usually no chemo
nodes.description: Fully staged early mucinous carcinoma is often managed with surgery alone.
bullets: Complete surgical staging with appendectomy
Observation is reasonable for fully resected low-risk early-stage disease
Enter surveillance after treatment

nodes.name: Mucinous advanced
nodes.title: Mucinous, advanced / high-risk: chemotherapy by primary type
nodes.description: Advanced mucinous carcinoma may follow a gynecologic or a colorectal-type backbone, individualized by the confirmed primary.
bullets: Carboplatin + paclitaxel, or a fluoropyrimidine-oxaliplatin (colorectal-type) regimen
Colorectal-type regimen has no dose protocol here - physician arranges it
Individualize by confirmed primary site and receptor / HER2 findings
Enter surveillance after treatment

nodes.name: Non-epithelial type
nodes.title: Non-epithelial: tumor family
nodes.description: Germ-cell and sex-cord stromal tumors follow entirely different management from epithelial disease; choose the family.
bullets: Malignant germ-cell tumors: young patients, fertility-sparing surgery, cisplatin-based chemotherapy
Sex-cord stromal (granulosa-cell) tumors: surgery, inhibin as a marker, chemo for advanced disease

nodes.name: Germ-cell
nodes.title: Malignant germ-cell tumor: fertility-sparing surgery + BEP
nodes.description: Most malignant ovarian germ-cell tumors are managed with fertility-sparing surgery and cisplatin-based (BEP) chemotherapy.
bullets: Fertility-sparing surgery (unilateral salpingo-oophorectomy) with staging
BEP (bleomycin-etoposide-cisplatin) chemotherapy for most tumors beyond stage IA
Follow tumor markers (AFP, beta-hCG, LDH) for response and surveillance
No dose protocol for BEP here - physician arranges the regimen

nodes.name: Sex-cord stromal
nodes.title: Sex-cord stromal (granulosa-cell) tumor: surgery +/- chemo
nodes.description: Sex-cord stromal tumors are managed surgically, with systemic therapy reserved for advanced or recurrent disease.
bullets: Surgery (fertility-sparing when appropriate) with staging
Inhibin / anti-Mullerian hormone as tumor markers
Chemotherapy (platinum-based) or endocrine therapy for advanced / recurrent disease
No dose protocol for these regimens here - physician arranges them
